story.headline: Stocks fall, with Technology the weak spot; small caps surge
story.lede: The S&P 500 is -1.4%, the Nasdaq -2.8%, the Dow -0.1% and the Russell 2000 -0.1%. 328 of 503 S&P 500 stocks are up. Futures point lower (-1.38%).

points.lead: Index read: S&P -1.4%, Nasdaq -2.8%, Dow -0.1%, Russell 2000 -0.1%.
points.body: Small caps are outrunning large caps. That usually means falling yields or improving growth expectations, because small companies borrow more and are more rate-sensitive.

points.lead: Sectors: Cons. Staples leads (+3.0%), Technology lags (-3.5%).
points.body: Defensive and rate-sensitive sectors lead while small caps outperform, which fits easing yields more than a flight to safety.

data.bottom: The economic readings lean negative. 0 improved and 7 worsened in the latest releases. Readings that move prices and growth in the wrong direction at once (higher inflation with weaker hiring) are the hardest mix for the Fed and for stock valuations.

rows.why: Inflation sets the Fed's path. Faster price growth means higher-for-longer rates, which is a headwind for stock valuations.
Core strips out food and energy and shows underlying price pressure, the part the Fed can actually influence.

rows.read: The labor market is loosening (up from 4.1%).
rows.why: A rising jobless rate shows demand for workers cooling. Modest rises ease inflation; fast rises signal recession risk.
Hiring pace drives income and spending. Thin payroll growth raises recession odds even as it eases Fed pressure.
Retail sales track consumer demand, the largest part of GDP and a driver of company revenue.
Weekly layoff filings are the fastest-moving labor indicator. Sustained increases warn of a turn.
Consumer mood tends to lead spending. Low readings usually mean cautious shoppers.
